::: {#rem-conditional-contradiction}
#### Proving a conditional by contradiction

To prove "if $P$, then $Q$" by contradiction,
suppose its negation, which is "$P$ and $\neg Q$" (@thm-negate-conditional):

> | Suppose $P$ and $\neg Q$.
> | $\vdots$
> | Therefore $C$ and $\neg C$.

A proof by contrapositive (@rem-contrapositive-template) assumes only $\neg Q$,
and has the fixed goal $\neg P$.
A proof by contradiction assumes both $P$ and $\neg Q$,
and any contradiction will do.

:::
